profile_text.body:
Credo AI describes itself as an AI governance platform company founded in 2020. According to its website, the company says it created the AI governance category and now focuses on what it calls Agent Governance, offering a registry for every agent plus agentic risk and controls. The platform is built on a Knowledge Graph that the company says fuses global regulatory intelligence with a customer's business context, and it is supported by forward-deployed governance experts. Credo AI says the platform lets enterprises discover their AI, enforce policy, manage AI risk, and achieve what it calls Measurable Trust across agents, applications, models, and AI vendors.

The company's tracked product is the Credo AI platform itself, listed under AI governance and risk management platforms. Per the site, it includes pre-built policy packs with regulatory intelligence for the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO 42001, and other standards, automated workflows, and audit-ready evidence. Credo AI also offers GAIA (Govern AI Assistant), which it says is generally available in the platform and compresses weeks of governance work into hours. The site claims native integrations across existing systems, with business context drawn from more than 300 integrations, and quotes customers including Mastercard and IBM.

The held facts add little beyond the profile: the company was founded in 2020, its website is credo.ai, and no lawsuits or MCP servers are recorded.
